title: GSTR-3B: what it is and why it matters

sections.heading: What is it?
text: GSTR-3B is the summary GST return in which you **pay your GST**. You report your total sales, the tax credit you claim on purchases (input tax credit), and pay the difference. Much of it is filled in for you from your GSTR-1 and from GSTR-2B (the statement of credit from your suppliers).

sections.heading: Who has to file it?
text: Businesses registered under the regular GST scheme, even for a period with no business at all (then as a nil return). The app shows it when your profile says "Regular" GST. Composition-scheme businesses file CMP-08 instead.

sections.heading: How often, and for which period?
text: Monthly, or quarterly if you are in the QRMP scheme. In QRMP you still pay tax for the first two months of each quarter with a separate challan. The due date is shown on this page and in your calendar; under QRMP it depends on the state of your principal place of business.

sections.heading: What happens if it is late or skipped?
text: Late filing brings a late fee, and tax paid late brings interest. A GSTR-3B cannot be filed before the GSTR-1 of the same period, and later returns wait for the missing ones.

sections.heading: Filing it yourself vs. with a CA
text: Filing it yourself is reasonable when your sales and purchases are simple and your GSTR-1 is filed. A CA helps when the tax credit in GSTR-2B does not match your purchase records.
